a new and practical profile of R & D is needed to support the management of R & D in systems engineering.

a new profile of R & D is introduced that is practical and useful for systems engineering firms, that the profile is one of four types, and that the portfolio map can be used to visualize the profile over time.

a new and practical way to profile R&D projects in systems engineering is introduced, which can support management efforts in characterizing and assessing an R&D portfolio for its contribution and fit to ongoing systems engineering efforts.

the management of systems engineering R & D projects, and our results provide a new and practical way to profile these projects.
how to manage R & D in a systems engineering environment.
the management of R & D for systems engineering and the development of a set of profiles to characterize the R & D projects in an R & D work program.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a systems engineering R & D portfolio is a set of R&D projects, each of which can be profiled as targeting, reinforcing, remodeling, or enabling the systems engineering work.

a systems engineering R & D portfolio should be profiled using a combination of profiles, including the new program positioning profile, to provide a balanced and holistic assessment of the R & D portfolio.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a systems engineering R & D portfolio is best managed with multiple profiles, each with its own focus.
the systems engineering R &D activity can be characterized by multiple profiles, each of which provides an important perspective for management.
the new profile and portfolio mapping approach can help managers to characterize the contribution of R & D to systems engineering work and to identify and address gaps in the portfolio.

a portfolio of R&D projects is more likely to be managed effectively if the projects are profiled in terms of their contribution to the ongoing systems engineering work program.
the systems engineering discipline is not a monolithic entity and that the R & D portfolio of a systems engineering firm must be managed accordingly.
the R & D activity in systems engineering should be profiled using a variety of complementary perspectives to support management efforts to achieve desired outcomes.
